title: Useful & Convenient
body: I bought my Oura ring in store and sized using the sizers at the store. Prior to purchasing my Oura ring I was an avid Apple Watch user to track my cycles and activity. I spoke with several people in my life who had used their Oura ring for over a year and they all said they stopped using the watch to track cycles and activities when they got their Oura. Im almost two months into using my Oura ring and I too have stopped using my watch for anything other than text, calls and time. The ring is extremely comfortable and the only time I don’t wear it is when I shower or use my hands to touch meat or mix when cooking. I like the apps interface as well. I will say Oura ring and app is probably not for people who hate looking at data points or following data trends. If you just like easy to read for the day then I’d stick to a watch. I bought the silver ring because after watching several review videos the gold and rose gold all faded. I wear my ring when I do my reformer workouts, washing dishes, carrying my kids, vacuuming and all the stuff. It has extremely tiny scratches that I can only see if I out a flash light on the ring. It also shines up easily with a quick wipe. Battery life is also amazing. I can easily go 5-6 days before I need to charge it and thats not because it’s dead but just low battery. Usually I pop it on the charger every 2-3 days when I get ready in the morning so it doesn’t ever really reach low battery and manufacturer suggest doing it that way. Overall love my purchase and highly recommend it. It does require a subscription fee to use the app so if you are going to purchase the Oura ring keep in mind you pay either a monthly fee or annual fee.

Keep the fee and the ring placement in mind before purchasing. title: I say its worth the value!
body: Definitely get the sizing kit. It makes a big difference and it’s better to wear the test ring out for a bit before actually buying the real one (I know, patience isn’t one of my finer qualities either). I’ve had mine for two weeks now and I love it. I move it between a few fingers from time to time just to switch it up, but keep it predominantly on the pointer finger on my non-dominant hand. I bought silicone covers for it to wear during the day because I do not have the ceramic one and it prevents it from scratches. If you get a regular one, it does scratch easy, which is why I only gave it four out of the five stars. It honest to goodness can tell me when I’m stressed! It has been on point each time! It’s making me more mindful of my activities during the day as well. You do need a membership annually in order to take full advantage of the app, but from what I can see it seems to be worth it. One of the best perks that no one has talked about in any reviews that I’ve read is that the Oura app itself has a section that provides you with meditations and breath work to help you learn to work through stress or get to sleep. I like those a lot! Battery life has been good as well. I typically don’t wear it in the shower and can stick it on the charger during that timeframe and it’s good to go. All in all, I definitely recommend!

title: Oura
body: Great health data, but the design, width, and lack of style options hold it back I’ve been using the Oura Ring daily for sleep and recovery tracking. The health insights are detailed and genuinely helpful, but the physical design and price make it hard to justify. What works well The sleep, HRV, and recovery data are accurate and easy to understand. The app is clean and gives useful daily guidance. Battery life is strong for something you wear 24/7. Where it falls short The ring is much wider and bulkier than expected, especially if you prefer slimmer, more feminine jewelry. It’s noticeable and not comfortable for all‑day wear. The gold finish scratches easily, which makes it look worn quickly. At $499 plus a subscription, the value doesn’t match the physical design. There are very limited style options. It would be great to see slimmer designs or versions with jewels or more elevated detailing, especially at this price point. Bottom line The Oura Ring delivers excellent health data, but the width, comfort, and lack of design variety make it hard to recommend at the premium price. It’s useful, but the style options need to evolve for it to feel worth it.

title: Terrible product with worthless customer service
body: I want to share my experience because prior to getting my ring, I’d heard nothing but good things about Oura. I was gifted the ring for Christmas by my husband and after 30 days, my ring still wasn’t tracking stress or resilience and it continued to say “calibrating” for Chronotype as well. I reached out to tech support, which is really just an AI chatbot, and they tried to put the blame on me by saying I needed to wear the ring more consistently and that maybe I’m moving around too much. I got frustrated and asked to be connected to a human. I was supposedly connected with a human, but I have my doubts — they give you the same canned responses as “Finn” the chatbot. Whatever the case, customer care asked me to provide screenshots, uninstall and reinstall the Oura app, and soft reset. If after 24 hours it still wasn’t working, I could reach back out. Well, unsurprisingly, that didn’t work. So I went through the whole customer care thing again, having to explain my situation from scratch. Again, I was asked to provide screenshots. Again, I was asked whether I was wearing my ring consistently. This time, they asked me to do a soft reset and a hardware reset where I docked my ring and tapped it firmly on the counter. Again, I was assured this would fix things and it had no effect. I reached out yet again and had to explain my situation. Every time, I am asked to provide screen shots and troubleshoot with the same tactics.This time, customer care asked me to do this convoluted reset where I dock my ring, turn it upside-down, and wait for the light to turn different colors. I legitimately thought the tech support agent was messing with me. This time, I explain my frustration with continually having to start from scratch with a new agent each day and they finally provide me with a reference number (which NO OTHER AGENT THOUGHT TO DO). Naturally, this also doesn’t work, so I reach out again with my reference number handy the following day and I’m told someone from the “technical team” will be reaching out to me because it’s not something that the member care team can help with. Two days pass, no email. I reach out again. Customer care says they will “escalate the issue”. Finally today after five interactions with the customer care team giving me the absolute run-around, I get an email from “Joseph with Oura” explaining that “after running a comprehensive diagnosis and checking your device's hardware status, I've found that your Oura Ring is functioning properly and is registering both Stress and Resilience levels, even though they may not be displaying in the application.” He goes on to say that I need to wear my ring more and - you guessed it — can I send screenshots so he can better assist me? You’ve got to be kidding me. To add insult to injury, he says he’ll be adding “one complimentary month of Membership to [my] account.” I’m so livid at this point — I told my husband to just dispute the credit card charge entirely because it’s obvious they aren’t interested in resolving this issue at all. Stress and resilience are basic metrics that were promised with this device and it straight-up doesn’t work. Along the way, I’ve been told by customer service that maybe I move around too much (I move around a normal amount for the type of health conscious individual interested in a ring marketed for tracking health metrics), my hands are too cold (my hands are a normal temperature), or my ring isn’t sized properly (it is — I used the ring sizing kit to get a snug fit). They’ve tried to pin the blame on me at every opportunity. Look, Oura -- this is unacceptable for a device that is nearly $400. If I'd known that the only information I'd be able to glean from my ring is my sleep data and HRV, I would've stuck with an Apple watch which has better activity tracking anyway. Not impressed and will not be recommending to anyone. TLDR; My oura ring has never tracked stress or resilience. Customer care says “too bad” and refuses to resolve; they won’t even send out a replacement unit.

title: Phenomenal Sleep Tracker With a Terrible Battery
body: I bought this in January 2025 and it truly improved my life. For me, my sleep and mental health are very dependent on each other. I found the sleep tracking and insights offered to show me what I was doing that was helping my sleep and where I could improve. Overall I find the app to be very useful. The longer I’ve worn it, the better it’s gotten to know me and my quirks. The data and insights provided get very good over time. Battery life was good until it wasn’t. More on that to follow. It’d be an easy 5/5 if the battery life didn’t fall off a cliff after less than a year. For the first 10 months, I could easily go a week between charges. I’d go on vacation and not even bring my charger because I wouldn’t need it. After that, battery life has continued to get steadily worse. After a year and a month, I’m lucky to get 3 days. I fully charged my ring 3 days ago at 9pm. It’s now 3pm and my ring is completely dead. Charge time is still about an hour. I find it frustrating to need to be charging it every other day to avoid the possibility of it dying on me. I never planned on writing a review as I am very happy with the ring and app overall. The battery life plummeting was annoying and something I’d deal with. Oura releasing a $100 charging case changed my mind. The Oura ring 4 was designed with planned obsolescence in mind. It’ll be just as described for about a year and then battery life will plummet. Interestingly enough, the standard warranty is one year. Maybe you bought the extended warranty. Probably not as it’s a ring. Not much can go wrong with it. Or why not buy the $100 charging case to solve a problem they caused. I’m sure the hope is that you upgrade to one of the new ceramic rings. I still love my Oura ring and wear it daily. It continues to learn more about me and becoming even more useful, it’s also started to unexpectedly die fairly frequently. That’s caused it to miss things that would’ve been useful to capture. I’m not sure how much longer I’ll continue to wear it. I’ll certainly replace it with another smart ring and it won’t be an Oura. In summary I do not recommend buying an Oura ring. When you spend several hundred dollars on a smart ring, the battery life shouldn’t fall 50% in a year. It’s a fantastic product. I love the way it fits, looks, and feels. Despite that, the significant decrease in battery life has left me incredibly disappointed.

I’ll share an update once I hear back from Oura and plan to provide a longer-term review after more time with the ring. For a premium product, this level of instability is disruptive to the overall experience. The only way to re-pair the ring after it disconnects is by using the charger, and without re-pairing, the app doesn’t even show your historical data. Overall, this has been a frustrating experience and falls short of what I expected.

title: Smart ring useful for tracking some health stats, but many you may already have on your phone.
body: This version of the Oura works OK, but I probably won't renew my subscription. I purchased this mostly to track my sleep.  I'm not a runner or much of an athlete these days, and all of my exercise tracking can be handled by my phone and watch for the most part, but they need to be re-charged daily, so I can't really track my sleep unless I want to carry around multiple chargers. I thought the ring would solve this issue, and for the most part it does.  Sleep tracking is accurate for the most part, but since I frequently nap or have my sleep interrupted by life, the ring doesn't always pick up on my catnaps or understand that I went back to sleep later in the night. My main issue with the ring is the comfort.  The ring sizer said I was size 11, but the sizer and the ring are not made of the same material, so I would recommend getting a half size larger, if that were possible.  The ring is also thicker than many rings so I find it annoying between my fingers.  I rarely forget that it's there, and I frequently find myself fiddling with it during the day. Setting up the charger is needlessly finicky in my opinion, since you have to line up the dimple with the light on the charger or nothing happens.  Fortunately the LED lights up when you get it right, but it's slightly delayed.  This is a minor issue, since you get used to the process soon enough.  I really despise proprietary chargers. My other complaint is the lack of notification about the battery level.  I think twice I went a couple of days with a ring that had no charge and didn't notice it, so I lost those days' data.  Maybe this is a me issue and not an Oura issue, so I may have to look into changing the settings somewhere. This would be a better product with a longer battery life and a thinner band.  It does track my sleep well enough, but it seems like a lot to pay for the subscription if that's the only feature I'm using. Another issue is one I had with a smart band I had previously and returned.  You have to look at your phone to find out anything, and once you're on your phone you have all the other distractions at hand.  If the lights on the inside of the ring could be used for information, this might be a better choice for me.

title: Great data, once you're past the paywall. Battery degrades FAST, but warranty support is great
body: This has transformed how I view and evaluate my personal health. I love the form factor - I rarely notice its presence, and it lets me wear a regular watch instead of having to always sport around a smartwatch. Battery life was great when I first got it, but after less than a year it only lasts about a day and a half. I like the stealth finish, but BE WARNED: the DLC coating WILL scratch the life out of any glossy surface you use - including your phone screen. ESPECIALLY your phone screen. Wearing this and carrying a phone without a screen protector is a recipe for disaster. Setup was effortless, despite receiving a previously-paired (used) item. The factory reset was easy enough but I wish I had known ahead of time that I was receiving a used product. As I mentioned, the battery longevity leaves quite a bit to be desired. Brand new, I could easily get a week out of it. 10 months later? recharge notifications every other day. Fortunately, all I had to do was go to the AI chatbot on Oura's site, tell it my ring battery sucked, and it pulled the battery health from my account logs. It saw that the battery was draining fast and immediately asked for my address for the replacement. Didn't have to talk to a single person. So big kudos for that. Also, this WILL 100% guaranteed get scratched, no matter what finish you end up with. In reality, the first few scratches will bother you because it's your shiny new expensive health toy, but after a few weeks you stop caring. even scratched to the heavens and back, it doesn't look terrible. One other benefit to note - recently the news has had increasing reports of smart ring batteries swelling while the user is wearing it, getting it stuck on their finger. The Oura Ring does NOT seem to have that problem. All of the affected units used plastic or epoxy inner rings, allowing the battery to breach the ring. Both the inner and outer rings of the Oura Ring are titanium; there is a gasket fitting between the segments that allows the battery to vent in case of failure, but it should not be possible for the battery to exert enough pressure on the titanium inner ring to get it stuck on your finger in a catastrophic failure mode. Overall functionality: +4/5 Subscription: -1/5 Battery degradation: -3/5 Warranty Support: +3/5 Wont destroy my finger: +1/5

title: 1 Month Post Purchase Review
body: Overall, I love it. I’m gonna break down my review as to why I love it and based on what you’re looking for in a smart ring to determine if this is a good fit for you. First, appearance. It doesn’t look masculine and is fairly scratch resistant. With any jewelry, you’re going to have a little scratching on the underside if you do anything with your hands. There’s plenty of protection options if that’s something you want to look into, but honestly I’ve had minimal scratching and it doesn’t bother me. It fit closer to my actual ring size, but you need to get sized to figure out your actual size. Oura offers a $10 you can order, but I personally just went to Best Buy and got my size off the display there. I believe Target also has sizers in the Oura display. But you do need to get fitted to know if the sensors are at an optimal location for best readings. Next category is App Quality. I really like the app and the reliability of the data it provides. I am not a super intense workout person, so it is perfect for my low impact workouts. I’ve heard people say it doesn’t provide accurate HR readings in higher intensity workouts, I see some improvement for that as you can have it track live HR data. I know a lot of people complain about the subscription and I just want to clarify that because I looked at that myself. The annual subscription is $69.99, monthly is $5.99. You can use the tracker without a subscription, however it gives you very basic data feedback. It tracks the basics, but does not give you pointers for improvement or how to better your scores.  With the subscription, you’re not only paying for the insights, but you’re also paying for the access to Oura Advisor, the AI integration that can give even further insights to the data you have logged in app and the feature to simply take a photo of a meal for meal logging. Women’s Health: I personally like it. I have used Apple Health for many many years so it’s my primary for reliability in start dates, but I like the detailed data with Oura. I think with further use of the Oura I might 100% convert to it but for now I can’t decide which I like better. Given my current medical, this is a fantastic tool for me. Tags has been the best way for me to tie symptoms to more probable causes rather than wondering and guessing or assuming. I was most drawn to that feature, but you have to remember to add the tags for it to be most effective. If simple tracking without a bulky smartwatch is more what you’re looking for, this will definitely do that for you but cheaper alternatives can do the same if you’re looking to save some money. If you have more complex medical and want the data insights to your health and be more in tune with your body, you want the Oura ring with a subscription. The good news is that you can actually use an FSA / HSA for both the ring and the subscription. Mine gave me almost no trouble as far as documentation when I purchased them.

title: Oura is incredible. Fully impressed.
body: Tech Insider Network Member The Oura fitness ring has been one of the most exciting pieces of fitness tech that I have used in quite a long time. A lot of this has to do with the fact that the ring itself is not cumbersome like other wearables and if you are used to wearing a ring or wedding band then it is unobtrusive. There is a lot to love about the Oura ring so let us get into it. Before you buy the Oura ring, Oura sends you ring sizes to try on to fine the perfect fit for your needs. These are really well made and sturdy trial rings of varying sizes. Once I found the proper ring size, I received my ring in stealth, which happens to be a beautiful color. The ring fits identical to my other wedding bands and is super comfortable. I have now worn my Oura ring for a little over one week and have not taken it off (Except to charge it ONCE....thing about that). The battery life is incredible and I get roughly 4.5 days out of it with full time use. The app and the data that Oura puts out is incredible. I love understanding my sleep and HRV because Oura will give you your readiness level which is almost on par with how I feel. So when I am going to workout, I know that my body has more to give. I have worn this while going on walks, cycling and weight lifting and when I tell you how incredible this ring and app is at identifying the workout; it is not only incredible but mind blowing. The Oura app will give you data at the top stating how long the workout was, Heart Rate averages and calories burned but it will actually suggest to you what workout it was and you can confirm it or change it. The mind blowing thing to me is the ring has been correct every single time be it weight lifting, cycling, walking, etc. It is super impressive. I also really like how Oura will baseline your vitals and then use that as the benchmark the more you wear the device. It is rather incredible for a small wearable, let alone a ring. I can honestly say that I can see myself owning multiple iterations of Oura and I have already highly recommended it to numerous people. title: Has a nice ring to it
body: Tech Insider Network MemberTop 1000 Contributor Glad to say I’m pleasantly surprised here. I’m not a jewelry guy, a relatively healthy man in his thirties, and already have a smart health watch, so it was a long shot to take the plunge into a health ring, but I’m glad I did. Using Oura’s ring sizing kit is recommended as the ring sizes are similar but slightly different than a normal ring. It was easy to use and helped me easily pick my size (11). As for the ring itself, I selected the black coating which looks sleek and is my favorite color, so thumbs up there. Out of the box, packaging looks impressive with the ring and charging base included. The ring fit as expected from the sizing chart and my wife was shocked at how lightweight it was. I hardly notice I’m ever wearing it and can’t stand wearing jewelry so that has been a pleasant surprise. Past just fitting on your finger, the hardware starts and stops there, but that’s where the software comes into play. Normally I’d complain about app associated software but with the ring, it’s a no brainer as the ring is useless without the app. Setup was easy but took a tad longer than expected, nothing I’d dock them for. The app is designed to track health metrics and also tied into other health apps such as the iOS app, and even brings in data from my orange theory band. Makes it REAL easy to use. I decided to take a chance and turn on push notifications which I’m not sure that I’ll keep on but again, I’m pleased with how non invasive that is. They basically only notify me to prep for bed, when I hit my activity goal, and when the battery is low. The app tracks more than I could list but learning about my heart rate, recovery rate, rest cycles and quality has all been very interesting and easy to track. The only two downsides here (and one is my fault), is that while this is waterproof and solid, one of the warnings is to not wear the ring while lifting weights as it may damage the exterior. I figured I’d have some leeway and could be careful… nope. First workout when I lifted weights, even carefully, it scratched off some of the black exterior. It’s unfortunate but DO NOT WEAR THIS WHEN LIFTING WEIGHTS! Secondly, the battery is relatively unimpressive. I figured it’d last for weeks or even a month at a time but the battery barely lasts six days. Charging takes a few hours but it’s annoying nonetheless. Either way, the pros easily outweigh the benefits and as long as the paint finish and batter my can stay in tact, I’ll plan to use this for years to come! See more
